subject: Aurora Systems — integration feasibility and validation plan
messages:
From: Kevin Park <kevin@aurora-sys.com>

Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0500
Subject: Intro + request: Redwood integration feasibility

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick chat this morning. As mentioned, Aurora Systems is evaluating a lightweight connector to Redwood Inference for our document ingestion pipeline (extract -> embed -> index -> semantic search). We want to surface a reference design and a short validation plan to make sure latency and privacy controls meet our enterprise customers' requirements.

High level asks:
- Example reference architecture for a hosted vs private deployment (we run in GCP)
- Guidance on model variants you recommend for dense retrieval embeddings + reranking at 1–3k concurrent queries
- Any known constraints around prefix caching / KV behavior with long-context inputs (customers may push 8k+ token docs)
- A smoke test plan (what Aurora should validate in first 2 weeks)

Attaching our integration spec draft. Happy to schedule a technical deep-dive next week.

(Attachment: aurora-integration-spec-v1.pdf)

Best,
Kevin Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Aurora Systems
kevin@aurora-sys.com

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro + request: Redwood integration feasibility

Thanks Kevin — great to meet today. I copied Jonas (our partner lead) so he can help coordinate the scope and commercial side.

We can absolutely put together a concise reference design and a focused validation plan. Preliminary notes:
- For embeddings we typically recommend our quantized embedding models for cost-sensitive dense retrieval; for high-recall scenarios, a 2-tier approach (cheap embeddings + lightweight reranker) works well.
- Long-context docs: our runtime supports KV caching and chunked prefixing; tail latency can increase with >4k effective context if customers query with full doc windows — we should validate with your median doc length and query patterns.
- Hosted vs Private: security and egress controls differ; Private (VPC) gives you KMS/HSM and auditable logs. We'll call out the exact differences in the reference doc.

Can Jonassuggest two 45-minute slots next week for an engineer-to-engineer deep-dive? Kevin, any preference for hands-on test environment (we can spin a short-lived dedicated instance or share a private sandbox)?

Thanks,
Soji (Sooujin) Lee
Senior Partner Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is our finalized test matrix (focused on largest enterprise customers) and a small dataset sample for the smoke tests. A few clarifications from our side:

Kevin / Ellie — thanks for the details and the test matrix. Summary of next steps and the validation plan we will execute with Aurora: 

Validation plan (summary):
- Week 0 (pre-checks): review sample corpus + confirm GCP project/service account scopes; baseline model selections
- Week 1 (Redwood labs): run hosted-sandbox tests focusing on embedding throughput and p95 latency; measure token cost and memory footprint; capture KV cache hit-rate for multi-doc flows
- Week 2 (Aurora-run): hand over artifacts and scripts (Terraform + test harness) for Aurora to execute in their GCP project; we will run parallel smoke tests from a private instance for parity

Recommendations (initial):
- For cost/latency balance, start with the q-embed-v2 for dense retrieval; pair with a lightweight 8-bit reranker (r-rerank-small-q8) for top-50 re-ranking
- Given 3k burst targets and 7.5k docs at p90, we recommend Dedicated capacity for production; sandbox can use hosted or short-lived dedicated nodes tuned to your concurrency pattern

Artifacts we will deliver by Monday EOD: reference architecture doc, Terraform for sandbox infra, a runnable test harness, and a small runbook for troubleshooting. I attached the initial runbook and the Aurora test matrix we received.

Attachments: aurora-test-cases.xlsx, redwood-reference-design-aurora.zip

Proposed deep-dive: Mon Nov 16, 2026 14:00–14:45 PT (engineer-to-engineer). Jonas will send calendar invite.

If any of the recommendations look off, flag before Monday so we can adjust.

Thanks,
